ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows an NPN transistor common-collector (emitter follower) circuit, with the collector connected to +15 V, the base directly driven by the input source labeled Vin, and the emitter node led out and labeled Vout, while also connected to ground through a 1.5 kΩ resistor. Reasoning: When a standard silicon NPN transistor is conducting, the base-emitter voltage is approximately VBE = 0.7 V. Because this is a common-collector circuit, the output is taken from the emitter, so the emitter voltage is approximately equal to the base input voltage minus VBE. Given Vin = 7.8 V, therefore Vout = Vin - VBE = 7.8 - 0.7 = 7.1 V.
